topic: Pilates for golfers: rotation without the pain

slides.headline: Stiff swing? Check your mid-back
slides.sub: Pilates ideas to rotate more freely through your whole body.

slides.title: Rotation should be shared
slides.body: A smooth golf swing spreads rotation through the hips, mid-back and shoulders. When one area is stiff, another often picks up the slack, and for many golfers that's the lower back.

slides.title: Open up your mid-back
slides.body: Try open books: lie on your side, knees bent, arms together in front. Rotate the top arm open as you breathe out, following it with your eyes. Eight slow reps each side.

slides.title: Let your hips turn too
slides.body: Lying on your back, let one knee fall out and back in, then try seated hip rotations. Hips that turn freely take load off the lower back through the backswing and follow-through.

slides.title: Control, not just range
slides.body: Pilates work like side planks, the saw and single-leg exercises on the reformer builds control through the trunk, so you can turn with speed without losing your posture.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: If pain lingers for more than a couple of weeks, wakes you at night, or travels down an arm or leg with pins and needles, have it assessed before ramping up your practice.

slides.headline: Want a golf-specific program?
slides.body: Our clinical Pilates team assesses how you rotate, then builds a program around your swing, on the mat or reformer. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Stiff swing and a sore lower back after 18 holes? Look a little higher up.

A smooth golf swing shares rotation between the hips, mid-back and shoulders. When the mid-back or hips are stiff, the lower back often picks up the slack.

Try open books for the mid-back, gentle hip rotations, and Pilates work like side planks and the saw to build control through the trunk. Aim for rotation you can control, not just more range.

If pain lingers for more than a couple of weeks, wakes you at night, or travels down an arm or leg with pins and needles, get it assessed first.

story.headline: Golfers: rotate from the middle
story.body: Open up your mid-back and hips so your lower back doesn't do all the turning. Try open books before your round.
